en: The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, one fascicle;
the translator’s name is lost, now appended to the Western Jin catalog.
Thus have I heard: The Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak near Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus.
The assembly consisted of forty-two thousand people;
including Samantabhadra, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, and others, numbering eighty-four thousand;
and Maitreya Bodhisattva and others, numbering one thousand from the Bhadrakalpa.
The Śakra kings and others, along with the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, were beyond counting;
the Brahmā kings and their various Brahmās were beyond counting;
and King Ajātaśatru, together with the many kings of Jambudvīpa, was beyond counting.

The Buddha was among his fourfold assembly of disciples—bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—and preached the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* (in the Han language, *Fahua*), with the Buddha reciting innumerable verses.
At that time, a stupa made of the seven treasures surged forth from the earth, rising as high as the Brahma Heaven.
In the center of the stupa was a great lecture hall made of the seven treasures, hung with banners, streamers, and flowered canopies, and purified by the fragrance of famous incense.
In the beautiful lecture hall there was a golden bed, and upon the bed sat a Buddha named Pao-hsiu-lo (in the Han language, "Great Treasure"), who praised Śākyamuni Buddha, saying: "Excellent! "
Excellent! Since my parinirvāṇa, more kalpas than the sands of the Ganges have passed, and I have remained in the midst of space across as many Buddha-fields as there are sands in the Ganges.
Although Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges have passed away, I have not returned to those fields throughout all those kalpas.

I have seen Śākyamuni Buddha diligently seeking the path to Buddhahood for the sake of all people; he practiced giving without weariness, never begrudging his hands, his eyes, his head, nor his wife, children, elephants, horses, or carriages, and he did not spare his precious treasures, being entirely free from any heart of greed or attachment.

I have come forth for this very purpose: desiring to make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha and to deliver those who are inferior, I pray that Śākyamuni Buddha will sit upon my golden throne and further preach the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*.
Thereupon, Śākyamuni Buddha ascended the lecture hall, took his seat upon the golden throne, and preached the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*. He further spoke innumerable verses, saying:
“Those who hear of the Buddha Ratnārāma and know his name shall not fear birth and death, nor shall they undergo further toil and suffering.”
"Whoever hears of the Buddha Bhaiṣajyarāja and knows his name shall not fail to be cured of their illness and shall personally recognize their past lives.
Thereupon, Śākyamuni Buddha spoke for incalculable asaṃkhyeya kalpas, and again spoke for incalculable asaṃkhyeya kalpas.

"When I was practicing the bodhisattva path, I sought out and bestowed the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* upon others; whatever I sought—be it food, drink, clothing, the seven treasures, or wife and children—I never harbored a heart of attachment."

“When I was a king, this world possessed an extremely long lifespan; I then installed my crown prince as king, abandoned the affairs of state, beat the drum and shook the bell, and proclaimed myself, saying:
‘Who wishes to take me as a slave?’”
"I seek the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*; I wish to practice its veneration.
At that time, a certain brāhmaṇa said to me:
"Come and be my slave, and I shall give you the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*."

I then followed the brāhmaṇa, serving him single-mindedly as a slave; I drew water, swept the ground, gathered flowers and fruits, and provided food and drink for the brāhmaṇa, never flagging for a thousand years.
The Buddha then spoke in verse:
"Beating drums and ringing bells, you make this vow: 'Who desires me?
Take me as your slave! I wish to practice making offerings."
"The slave’s heart was good and his conduct was virtuous.
The Buddha said:
"At that time, the king was my own self;"
At that time, the brahmin was Devadatta.
By whose grace did I attain the fulfillment of the six pāramitās, the thirty-two marks, and the eighty minor characteristics?
All of this is due to the merit and kindness of Devadatta.

Devadatta is my good teacher; it is through the kindness of my good teacher that I have attained the fulfillment of the six *pāramitās*, the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics, and the majestic power and nobility to deliver all beings throughout the ten directions—all of which is the grace of Devadatta.

After an incalculable number of kalpas, Devadatta shall attain Buddhahood; his name shall be Tishyaraśmirāja Buddha, and his land shall be named Tiheyue, which in the language of Han means "Land of Heaven and Earth."
The Buddha Tianwang shall preach the Dharma for the sake of sentient beings, never ceasing or wearying throughout the entire kalpa.

At his first preaching of the Dharma, he shall cause people as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to attain the path of Arhatship; people as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to attain the path of Pratyekabuddhahood; and people as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to resolve their minds toward Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
“At that time, the lifespan of the Buddha Devendra was twenty kalpas. After his parinirvāṇa, the Dharma remained for twenty kalpas.

Following the parinirvāṇa of the Buddha Devendra, his relics were not dispersed; instead, a single stūpa made of the seven precious gems was erected, sixty li wide and eighty li long. All the people of Jambudvīpa went there to make offerings to the Buddha’s relics.”

At that time, countless people attained the path of Arhatship; countless people resolved their minds toward Pratyekabuddhahood; and countless people resolved their minds toward Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
“Good sons and good daughters!

Having heard this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, those who believe it and do not slander it will extinguish their past and future sins, close the gates to the three evil realms, and open the gates to the three virtuous realms. They shall be foremost among those born in the heavens and foremost among those born as humans; they shall be born before the Buddhas of the ten directions, spontaneously arising by transformation within lotus flowers made of the seven precious jewels.”
Thereupon, a bodhisattva named Prajñākūṭa, who had come from the Buddha in the direction below, addressed his own Buddha, requesting to return early to his native land.
Śākyamuni Buddha said to him, “Prajñākūṭa!”
"I have a bodhisattva named Mañjuśrī; you may go to meet him and then return to your own land.

Immediately, Mañjuśrī emerged from the pool of the Dragon King Śaṅkha, seated upon a great lotus flower as large as a chariot wheel, with a thousand petals. He was accompanied by a vast multitude of bodhisattvas.
Mañjuśrī descended from the great lotus flower, paid homage to the two Buddhas, and returned to exchange greetings with the Bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa.
Prajñākūṭa asked Mañjuśrī, "How many beings were there in the pool you entered? What was their number?"
Mañjuśrī replied: "Their number is exceedingly great; no one is able to calculate it.
If it were to be spoken of verbally, it would not be believed by the mind; there shall naturally be witnesses."
At that moment, flowers immediately surged up from beneath the pool, all of which had been scattered throughout it.
For those who had originally resolved to attain the bodhicitta, the flowers remained in mid-air and spoke only of Mahāyāna matters;
for those who had originally resolved to become śrāvakas, the flowers remained in mid-air and spoke only of severing the cycle of birth and death.
Mañjuśrī, seeing the flowers in this manner, replied to the Bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa with these verses:
"According to your own understanding, distinguish their number for yourself."
The Bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa again asked Mañjuśrī,
“What kind of Dharma do you teach such that those delivered are so numerous? Mañjuśrī replied:
"Within this pond, only the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* is preached. Prajñākūṭa asked again:
"That Dharma is most honored and none can equal it; is there anyone who may readily attain Buddhahood through it?"
Mañjuśrī replied, "The Dragon King Sāgara has a daughter who is eight years old; her wisdom is immense and her aspiration is no small matter—she shall attain Buddhahood."

The Bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa said to Mañjuśrī, “I have observed your teacher seeking Buddhahood through diligent austerity and accumulating merit over a vast number of kalpas; I did not believe that this woman could attain Buddhahood so soon.”
A woman immediately emerged from within the pond, circumambulated the Buddha three times, joined her palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:

“The Buddha’s marks and signs are upright and sublime; your merit is towering and vast. You are honored by all the devas and revered by all dragons, spirits, humans, and *sattvas*. The Dharma you preach is most venerable. Now I establish this vow: I desire to attain Buddhahood.”
Śāriputra then said to the girl:

"Although you have made this vow, a Buddha cannot be attained [merely by that]; furthermore, as for you, a woman, though you have accumulated merit through your practice, your conduct has not yet reached the level of a bodhisattva."
The woman took a single maṇi jewel, worth an entire great kingdom, and quickly presented it to the Buddha; the Buddha also accepted it with equal swiftness.
The woman then asked Śāriputra and the Bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa:
"Was my gift of the jewel to the Buddha slow or fast?"
He replied, "Very swiftly!
The woman spoke again:
"Was the Buddha slow in accepting my pearl?
He replied, "Very quickly!"
The woman said, "I was slow in offering my pearl to the Buddha, and the Buddha was slow in accepting my pearl; now I shall take up the Buddha’s [form] with speed.

Thereupon, at that very moment, her body transformed into that of a Bodhisattva, and the entire assembly was struck with wonder; she then transformed into the body of a Buddha, fully endowed with all the primary and secondary marks of excellence.
The lands and disciples were as they had been under the Buddha’s guidance.
The entire assembly—including devas, nāgas, spirits, and countless humans—all resolved to attain unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment;
and the trichiliocosm shook in six ways.
Thirty thousand *srotāpannas* attained the stage of *avaivartika*.
The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*, one fascicle.
